A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, theoretical framework, and PUG experiments. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, proofs, figures, and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 6–7 report original PUG classification experiments comparing non-generative methods with generative search and replay.

after.justification: Section 5 retains original PUG experiments, while Appendix C adds original comparisons of decoder architectures in Table 2 and Figure 9.

M1.justification: The principal slot-based VAE, attention regularizer, encoder-initialized latent search, and generative replay objectives remain unchanged. The flexible Transformer and CNN architectures introduced in Appendix C serve as experimental controls rather than revisions to the main method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PUG-Background, PUG-Texture, and PUG-Object, covering unseen animal–background, animal–texture, and animal–animal combinations. The new appendix experiments use the existing PUG-Background task.

E2.justification: Appendix C introduces substantive comparisons against a flexible Transformer decoder and a CNN autoencoder with a monolithic latent representation. Conversely, v1 Figure 6C's PUG-Object comparisons using DINOv1, I-JEPA, CLIP, DINOv2, and SigLIP2 are absent from v3, which reports only models trained from scratch on that task.

E3.justification: The original splits and training settings in Appendix B are retained. The new Appendix C.2 comparison matches total latent dimensionality, uses three separate linear readouts for the CNN representation, and applies 750 search iterations to both architectures. These are additional experimental protocols, not established changes to the original experiments.

E4.justification: V3 adds direct tests of decoder inductive biases absent from v1. Appendix C.1 tests a Transformer with patch self-attention and no attention regularization; C.2 compares slot-based and monolithic-latent autoencoders before and after search. These investigate whether explicit decoder constraints and slot structure are necessary for the observed generalization.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose three random seeds and display uncertainty with error bars. V3 adds tables with plus/minus values, but does not introduce a different uncertainty-estimation procedure, increased run count, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds detailed ID/OOD entries in Table 1 and new decoder results: Table 2 reports 83.43% versus 78.53% OOD accuracy for constrained and flexible decoders, while Figure 9 reports search gains of 43.6 versus 6.0 percentage points. The supervised from-scratch PUG-Texture bar changes from approximately 53% to 65%; v3 identifies the Transformer result as 64.8%, without establishing a same-configuration improvement. Pretrained PUG-Object entries disappear. The original generative results in v1 Figure 7 are retained in v3 Figure 6.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, assumptions, Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2, and Appendix A proofs retain their mathematical substance. Appendix theorem renumbering and removal of a stray argument in the tangent-space expression are not substantive theoretical revisions.

C1.justification: V1's necessity framing and introduction's assertion that non-generative methods cannot achieve compositional generalization through inductive bias are substantially narrowed. V3 explicitly allows both paradigms to succeed in principle and centers its contribution on the relative simplicity of generative inductive biases, consistently revising the title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds substantive qualifications about confounded pretraining comparisons, computational overhead, non-invertibility under occlusion, interactions such as shadows and reflections, and approximate enforcement of theoretical assumptions. Appendix C also motivates new interpretations: flexible decoders may generalize through implicit biases, while slot structure appears important for substantial search gains.

D1.justification: V3 adds search/replay pseudocode in Figure 8, specifies additional PUG factors, clarifies that image accuracy requires all three labels to be correct, and explains the exclusion of Slot Attention from unsupervised experiments. It also documents the new controls and per-iteration computational costs. Existing hyperparameters and hardware disclosures are largely unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix D adds connections to Rombach et al., Peebles and Xie, Jaini et al., and Whittington et al. concerning scalable generative models and biologically motivated regularization. Section 6's principal positioning remains stable. Several other reference changes merely update existing preprints to published versions.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory argument, theoretical takeaways, experimental narrative, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Section 5.1 now separates training-from-scratch results from pretrained-encoder results, and new appendices organize additional experiments and extended discussion. These changes substantially revise the paper's explanatory structure.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main-text layout, adds Tables 1–2 and Figures 8–9, and redesigns the non-generative results display from three horizontal panels to two stacked panels alongside a table. The dataset montage moves from v1 Figure 5 to appendix Figure 7; the generative results figure is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V3 improves claim calibration by replacing the broad necessity framing with a comparative inductive-bias argument. Appendix C supplies useful checks of decoder structure, and Appendix D makes pretraining confounds, assumption failures, and computational costs explicit. These improve interpretation and transparency, although the added evidence remains confined to the existing synthetic setting and the pretrained PUG-Object comparison is lost. The net improvement is supported but limited.
